title: How do yall make such good games?
author: Polasomaipo
selftext: What is the actual process of making games with ai? Where do you start, how do you save your progress, how do you continue making them in another chat etc.

comments.author: Ok-Investment4414
comments.body:
cli like claude code , codex etc u can ideate in the chat make the plan and then the cli helps its helps keep shit organized and was made for that kinda workflow to execute .   
U can start by asking ai how to start and what it recommends. As for assets u can get them anywhere with a google search and the tool of choice or make them in stuff like blender by connecting blender to your chat or cli.Same for your engine of choice unit/unreal/godot/rpgm/renpy etc.  
Models used at higher efforts yield better results . But if u wanna be spoon fed ask your ai program test a bit then come back here for more info. 

That's not even an attack its more of we don't know what u dont know. Ai can get u up to speed and help with asking the right questions faster and more distilled.  But almost anyting u wanna make can be done as a basic prototype by a good frontier model at a high thinking level as a threejs html file. Chats also have a cloud version of the cli

comments.author: Weekly_Raise_781
comments.body:
some use ai studios to one shot their games, i've seen cool minecraft demos with this   
also chat prompted web games have been impressing, or you could use game engine mcp integration.  
art pipeline could be ex. prompt images of what you are interested in and then ask to make 3d model out of it.

I use more of a programmer pipeline with linear app to do project management, but you can use github issues for the same, then just give any ai connection to where your tasks are and tell it to do them, could also just be bunch of text files.   
Then AI does coding, pushing to version control, code review and bunch of tests are run automatically on local github runners to see if app crashes on launch, any errors on static analyzers, capture screenshots and post them to issues etc. I got claude max, gpt pro and devin max running all day and night and latest models last nicely compared to month ago. Smarter models can give sub tasks to cheaper models is a good way to save some tokens.

If you want I can give you links to test it 😊 if you are into MMORPG s ofc

comments.author: erratic_ostrich
comments.body:
1) pick an AI (I recommend claude because the new opus model is insane)

2) decide if you want to use an engine (unity/godot/unreal) or let the AI work from scratch. an engine will give you more control over anything but it has a learning curve, so it depends if you want to actually learn game development or just get a game done (both are valid)

3) write everything about your current game idea, the more detailed the better

4) show your idea to the AI and ask it the same questions you are asking here. I'm not being dismisive, it will give you a better answer for your specific. Ask what tools do you need, ask guidance to set them up, and ask for the ideal workflow

5) ???

6) profit

comments.author: yaosio
comments.body: A good game isn't made by AI...yet. A good game comes from implemting ideas, play testing them, band changing what doesn't work. You can not one shot a good unique game because AI doesn't know the pattern for fun yet. Once it does that's the end of vibe coding for non personal projects.

comments.author: _Raro
comments.body:
Rather than trying to one shot the basic idea first tell the AI to make a detailed game design document. 

I used Claude opus 5.5 my basic prompt when creating a new game is  "I want to make a game in godot 4.7.1 my game idea is \_\_\_\_\_\_\_ make a detailed game design document. Ask me any questions if you need clarification on anything"

Use godot. as the entire engine is open source the AI understands it much better.

Then when you start just tell the AI create the game in the design document.

comments.author: barret232hxc
comments.body: same process I've used for years developing games. Start out with a small prototype to test the mechanics. Fine tune the mechanics to see if it's even fun. and then iterate, iterate, iterate and spend 100's 1000's of hours polishing and refining the game until it feels good

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: The trick is to think like a gamedev. First build a Game Design Document (GDD). Put in there everything you want in the game. Then prompt while handing over your GDD.
